findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: people_search, find_people, fetch_email, verify_email · Private data: people_search, reveal_profile, find_people, find_company_emails, company_search, check_credits · Public sink: people_search, reveal_profile, find_people, fetch_email, find_work_email, verify_email, find_company_emails, reverse_email_lookup, find_linkedin_profile, find_email_from_linkedin · Destructive: verify_email.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: people_search, find_people, fetch_email, verify_email · Private data: people_search, reveal_profile, find_people, find_company_emails, company_search, check_credits · Public sink: people_search, reveal_profile, find_people, fetch_email, find_work_email, verify_email, find_company_emails, reverse_email_lookup, find_linkedin_profile, find_email_from_linkedin · Destructive: verify_email

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "people_search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
